title: Grateful Dead Live at The Warehouse on 1970-02-01
source: Lineage: Source 1 SBD > MSR > C > DAT (Biodtl thru O1(7:27); Source 2 MR > Revox A77 > tube pre (O1@7:27 thru Lovelight); Transfer info: Bottlehead tube tape pre pair Tesla tubes circa 1980  > Apogee Mini Me 24/96 > Apogee Mini DAC monitoring and mastering  > FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording (mostly solid mix aside from early balance quirks) captures a marathon Lovelight with Peter Green and a raging Other One.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its extended, loose‑grooving Lovelight featuring guest guitarist Peter Green trading licks with Jerry, plus an electrifying The Other One. Recording quality is generally good – a soundboard source that’s clear overall, though the first few tunes suffer from a slightly off mix and a vocal level bump. Fans also note lively banter and the late‑night Pigpen surge that stretches the set.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are 4‑5 stars, emphasizing standout performances and only minor recording balance issues, yielding a high combined show/recording score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mix is a bit off for the first couple of tunes (vocals up in mix, Bobby prominent), but overall clarity and balance are solid throughout the rest of the set.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The Lovelight extends the second half, giving the concert a looser, jam‑heavy feel; early acoustic moments are noted as less prominent this night, while stage banter adds extra flavor.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Trading licks with Peter Green during Lovelight – highlighted as a favorite Dead moment.
band_member_comments.Phil: Brief Dark Star riff mentioned, showing his improvisational spark early in the set.
band_member_comments.Bob: Early mix puts ‘Bobby’ (Bob Weir) forward in the soundstage.
